title: Who Coached OU Between Gary Gibbs and Bob Stoops? (1995-1998)
question: Who coached Oklahoma football between Gary Gibbs and Bob Stoops?
answer: Two coaches: Howard Schnellenberger led Oklahoma for the 1995 season and went 5-5-1, and former Sooner nose guard John Blake coached from 1996 through 1998 and went 12-22. Bob Stoops was hired on Dec. 1, 1998.
summary: Between Gary Gibbs and Bob Stoops, Oklahoma was coached by Howard Schnellenberger in 1995 and John Blake from 1996 to 1998. Here are the facts.
body: The four seasons between Gary Gibbs and Bob Stoops are a short chapter in OU history, but a trivia favorite. Two coaches filled that gap, each with a notable résumé.

First came Howard Schnellenberger, hired away from Louisville to replace Gibbs. He arrived with real credentials: his Miami team had won its first national title by beating Nebraska 31-30 in the Orange Bowl after the 1983 season. His 1995 Sooners opened 3-0 and climbed as high as No. 10 in the AP poll, and they tied Texas 24-24 in the Red River game. They finished 5-5-1, and Schnellenberger resigned on Dec. 18, 1995, after the first year of a five-year contract.

Next was John Blake, a familiar face. A graduate of Charles Page High School in Sand Springs, Blake had played nose guard for Barry Switzer from 1979 to 1982 and was later a Sooner assistant. He then coached the defensive line for the Dallas Cowboys during their Super Bowl-winning run in the 1990s. When OU named him head coach in 1996, he became the first Black head coach in any Sooner sport.

Blake's teams went 12-22 over three seasons, but his recruiting is widely credited with stocking the roster that Stoops led to the 2000 national championship. Blake died in 2020 at age 59. On Dec. 1, 1998, athletic director Joe Castiglione hired Stoops, and a new era began.
